newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Aviastar resumes work Monday.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Aviastar resumes work Monday.

text.p: Russia's AO Aviastar aircraft manufacturer will resume work again from Monday after a 10-week stoppage due to financial problems, a company official said on Friday.
Valery Savodchenko, head of Aviastar's international department, told Reuters that all staff would begin work from November 4 despite some problems remaining.
In August Aviastar sent about 28,000 workers on enforced holiday. But in mid-October a team of the plant's workers installed British-made engines on a Tupolev-204 jet.
"We have begun works to certificate the Tu-204 powered by engines from Rolls-Royce," Savodchenko said, adding that the jet had begun test flights.
He said Aviastar, based in the city of Ulyanovsk on the Volga, hoped the Tu-204 could be certificated in January 1997.
Rolls-Royce has supplied two engines for one Tupolev-204, but he did not say how many engines would be supplied in all.
Aviastar is one of Russia's biggest Russian aviation plants, manufacturing Tupolev cargo and passenger planes.
Egypt's Kato Group, which is diversifying into aviation, has ordered 30 Tupolev 204s, which it intends to fit with Rolls-Royce engines.
The deal to purchase the planes is worth $450 million, according to Middle East Economic Digest.
Under the terms of the deal, the Russian goverment must guarantee the return of part-payment by Kato for the planes if they are not delivered.
An official of the Aviaexport agency responsible for exporting Russian-made planes said on Friday that the guarantees would be given during next week.
